verdict.rationale: Aider lets developers ask natural-language questions about the codebase with /ask and AI? comments. It also feeds run and test failures back into the chat via /run and /test, and the docs mention requesting bug fixes; community users report it answers code-tracing questions well. However, no doc describes a dedicated debugging or troubleshooting workflow, and hands-on reports note subtle errors. missing for 10: dedicated debugging/troubleshooting documentation (e.g., stack-trace diagnosis walkthroughs), independent hands-on corroboration of bug diagnosis quality specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can debug issues and troubleshoot using natural-language queries

citations.quote: /ask Ask questions about the code base without editing any files.
You can use the /run command in the chat to run your code and optionally share the output with aider.
If there are test errors, aider expects the command to print them on stdout/stderr and return a non-zero exit code.
AI? triggers aider to answer your question.
Request new features, test cases or bug fixes using your voice and let aider do the work of editing the files in your local git repo.
Aider can answer questions I can't search for via LSP, like 'what code would process the following URL' and similar.
